Definition: from G1047 and G5438; a treasure-house, i.e. a court in the temple for the collection-boxes:--treasury.
BiblicalUsage: Gazophylakion is the treasury, the court in the temple where the offerings were kept. Jesus spoke in the treasury as He taught in the temple in John 8:20, and He sat over against the treasury in Mark 12:41 and watched how the people cast money in. The rich cast in much, and the poor widow cast in more than they all, says Mark 12:43. Luke saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury in Luke 21:1.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the treasury is where Jesus still sits and watches. He saw the rich and the widow, and He counted her two mites as more than their abundance. I hold that God measures the gift by the heart that gives it, not by the weight of the coin.
